messages.content: I want to buy apples, rice, and 12 pack of bottled water from a Walmart near San Jose. Show me the product information and stock availability.

function.name: walmart_purchase
function.description: Retrieve information of items from Walmart including stock availability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

product_list.description: Items to be purchased listed in an array.

pack_size.description: Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. Default is not use it if not specified.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function with location "San Jose" or maybe specify loc as "near San Jose". Provide product list ["apples", "rice", "bottled water"]? But we also have pack sizes; only bottled water has pack size 12. So pass pack_size [null,null,12] but default can omit unspecified ones.

Let's produce JSON:

{
    "loc": "San Jose",
    "product_list": ["apples","rice","bottled water"],
    "pack_size":[12]
}

But order matters: pack_size length equals product_list length. For first two no pack size needed so could set null or omitted? According to spec: If not used then don't include element. That means pack_size array may contain entries corresponding to each item where pack size applies. It says "The size of the array should be equal to product_list." Hmm contradictory. Let's just provide full array with None values for those without pack size: [None,None,12]. In python representation would be [0,0,12]? Actually they said default is not use it if not specified. Might mean you can leave out pack_size entirely if none apply. But here one does. We might supply pack_size=[12], but mapping ambiguous. I'd better follow spec: "size of the array should be equal to product_list." So I'll give [0,0,12].

Thus call function.
